official_sources.title: Practice guide 40 supplement 4: boundary agreements and determined boundaries

verified_claim_families: Registration with general boundaries is sufficient for most titles, while boundary agreements and determined boundaries address cases needing more precision.
A boundary agreement may address the legal boundary position, maintenance of a boundary feature or both.
Recording a boundary agreement in the register does not itself convert the boundary into a determined boundary.
Unless determined under section 60 of the Land Registration Act 2002, a registered estate boundary shown for register purposes remains a general boundary.
A determined boundary records the exact line after that line has been identified; HM Land Registry does not resolve the underlying disagreement about its location.
The title plan shows the general position of a determined boundary and a filed determined-boundary plan is retained for identifying the exact line.
INSPIRE Index Polygons are an open dataset covering locations of freehold registered property in England and Wales.
INSPIRE polygons form a subset of HM Land Registry Index Polygons for freehold land and property.
The INSPIRE service describes polygons as showing the position and indicative extent of a registered property.
Each INSPIRE polygon has a unique Land Registry-INSPIRE ID related to a registered title.
The INSPIRE dataset and metadata are published monthly.
INSPIRE polygon files are published in GML and require GIS software for viewing.
An indicative polygon cannot be promoted to an exact legal boundary without determined-boundary or equivalent authoritative evidence.
A candidate reference alone does not prove a current INSPIRE ID or title-plan linkage.
Candidate binding requires current official polygon bytes, title linkage and lifecycle evidence.
Current INSPIRE IDs and candidate-specific GML polygon bytes for the three seed candidates were not read back in this runtime.
